publication: Sebastiaan A. Terwijn, Generalizations of the recursion theorem, author-hosted 10-page manuscript dated December 16, 2019; paper published in Journal of Symbolic Logic 83(4) (2018), 1683–1690. This manuscript is distinct from The noneffectivity of Arslanov’s completeness criterion and related theorems.

reviews.checked_passages: Section 2 pp.2–3: definitions and Proposition 2.1 statement only. Section 3 pp.3–4: Theorem 3.1, Definition 3.2, full parameterized race proof including footnote, and uniform Theorem 3.3 with proof. Later sections are outside this review.
reviews.consumers: First-four-subarea readiness audit; no new entry adoption.
reviews.outcome: No defect found in the selected ADN proof. A corpus construction should specify a tie convention in the finite race and freeze the winning index before simulation. All prerequisites are present in uniform-self-reference and ordinary finite stages. The FPF-to-DNC converse can be a small Arslanov-entry extension: compile j(n) that waits for phi_n(n)=k and then simulates phi_k, and put g(n)=f(j(n)). Proposition 2.1 itself only states the equivalence and cites an external proof; no full proof-source audit of that proposition is claimed. The joint incomplete-c.e.-oracle generalization and applications to other numberings are not selected.

reviews.checked_passages: Adoption reuses the assessed §2 definition/Proposition2.1 statement and §3 Theorems3.1/3.3 proof including footnote.
reviews.outcome: ADN uses explicit request-first ties, a frozen output index and the actual earlier partial-family compiler. The FPF-to-DNC converse is an elementary corpus construction from ordinary universal evaluation/specialization, not an assertion that the source supplies its proof. No joint relative generalization.
